newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - June 27.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - June 27.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:
* Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$19.06 (-0.19)

BHP is expected to announce later on Friday morning its return to annual profit growth and mark the end of a painful earnings rut. The steel-making, mining and petroleum group is forecast, on average, to report a six percent rise in net profit before abnormals to around A$1.375 billion for the year ended May 31. Also BHP said on Thursday it would sell its Newcastle-based Electrolytic Managanese Dioxide Plant to Delta Industries Electrical Industries Ltd for A$57 million.

WMC Ltd said on Thursday that it expected its 1996/97 net profit to be in line with most market forecasts. It also said on Thursday its Kalgoorlie nickel smelter in Western Australia was operating at full capacity but a 42-day shutdown earlier this year would weigh on the group's profit for 1996/97 ending June 30.

Metal recycler Metalcorp Ltd said on Thursday it had agreed to buy Queensland-based Wanless Metal Industries Pty Ltd after rival Simsmetal Ltd was blocked from making a bid by the anti-monopolies regulator. Metalcorp did not reveal the purchase price but said the acquisition would include a share issue and would be earnings per share positive.

OPSM Protector Ltd said on Thursday it was examining potential acquisitions up to A$70 million, mainly for its Protector Technology division. OPSM was looking at targets from A$10 million up and could easily handle a debt-funded acquisition up to A$70 million, given its conservative balance sheet, managing director Jeff Kelly told reporters after a Securities Institute of Australia briefing.
* FH Faulding & Co Ltd FHF.A X A$7.50 (unch)

Pharmaceuticals group F.H. Faulding and Co Ltd said on Thursday that it was pleased with the 1996/97 year and expected to report higher profits. "Yes I think we have already said we are expecting modest growth," Faulding chief executive Ed Tweddell told reporters after an address to the Securities Institute of Australia.

Miner RGC Ltd said on Thursday it expected net profit for the 1996/97 (July-June) year to be less than half of the A$76.5 million achieved in the 1995/96 year. RGC said it also plans to write down A$50 million on the Thalanga base metals mine in Queensland and a A$30 million writedown on its Renison tin mine in Tasmania.
